newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's to revamp U.S. management - NYT.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's to revamp U.S. management - NYT.

text.p: McDonald's Corp plans to revamp the top management structure of its U.S. business in an attempt to improve profits and build its market share, the New York Times said.

In its Monday edition, the Times said an internal memo by McDonald's Vice Chairman Jack Greenberg, who heads the company's U.S. operations, said "we need to make fundamental changes in our business structure."
In the memo, Greenberg said that no dismissals, layoffs or wholesale relocations among the company's 5,000 headquarters and regional employees are expected.
The Times said the move is an effort to make the company less bureaucratic and more flexible.
The Times said that Greenberg has told franchisees that he will keep the company's system of 41 regional directors, but will replace McDonald's top U.S. administrators.

The eight current zones would be replaced by a smaller number of national divisions, each of which would operate more autonomously, the Times said. Each division would be headed by a president, who would be responsible and accountable for that unit.
